lines: You think you've got all the answers, you know,
but action? Still haven't we seen you just show.
You talk big plans like the sky's yours to fly,
yet when push comes to shove, you never even try.
You float through this room with your head in the air,
but you don't give a single damn or a care.
You've got grand ideas, but no backup plan,
just a mirror, a mic, and a ego-man.
You strut through the chat like it's all just your air,
and promise the moon without anyone to dare.
You speak like you're blazing, but there's no real flame,
just your ego repeating your own full name.
You strut in here like the room's just a seem,
your confidence's all in your head — just a dream.
You talk up your moves like you've got some class,
but you're just hot air with a side of sass.
You strut in like you got some divine flair,
but your big talk's just hot air.
All your "I could do better" claims,
amount to zero moves off the page or the frames.
You've got *your* way to do everything the wrong way,
but you swear up and down it's the best way, every day.
You're full of brass, blaring plans you'll never pass,
a one-star show with a sold-out cast—just you, no class.
You got a brain so full, it's crowding your mind,
you overthink each step before you even try to find.
At the campsite, while we grill, you're cross-checking what's been done,
but genius like yours needs more than just one sun.
You over-analyze every little think,
I'll drown my toast before I quote a textbook drink.
You've got a PhD in "but what's the head?"
Meanwhile, the cake's gone cold—again, all *your* dead.
Your brain's always spinning, a hurricane in your mind,
but ideas too big just leave you stuck behind.
You'd overthink a paper boat,
why don't you just let it float?
Oh sweet summer child with that Ivy League brain,
you could debate a toaster—and win, I'm not vain.
You overthink coffee orders, nearly drown
in your thoughts—this reunion's turning town.
You got a master's in "duh" and call it your brain,
debate the weather like it's a cold war campaign.
You trip just walking on flat sidewalk ground,
but everyone here's dumber than your soapbox has crowned.
You overthink life like a spider in think,
and turn small talk into conspiracy link.
Your brain's always spinning, a tornado in head,
so take a deep breath—this joke isn't dead.
You think your one-liners will make the crowd drop,
but your jokes are so thin I could toss them on a prop.
You nod and cackle like you're cracking every head,
but your punchlines land flat—literally, I'm half dead.
You tell a bad pun and the room wants to drop,
you air-tweet the laugh and clip your own crop.
The silence could kill and the vibe starts to die,
but you're still grinning like some tragic comedy guy.
You crack a joke so forced I'd rather hear hell,
you pause just long enough to hear yourself tell.
Your laugh lands first—before the crowd even sound,
you're headspace rich while we're still standing on ground.
You think every line's a punch, a lyrical drop,
but we just nod like props, faking a crop.
You cackle first, then shout "I told you I'd kill!"
but the only thrill here is escaping your hill.
You think every line's a punch, but it's just a bad bunch,
you're juggling hot air and your ego's a lunch.
The room echoes every "ha" with a collective groan,
you laugh so loud, you sit on your joke's cold throne.
You drop a cliché punchline, it ain't even a bit,
your humor's a costume you wear just for fit.
You cackle before the laugh even hits the crowd,
and yet you still act all cool when you're being proud.
You'd trade your life just to keep your grind alive,
your soul's been shelved so your hustle can survive.
You smile through smoke because you can't admit you can't see,
the finish line's gone—nice how you still sell it to me.
You're a self-proclaimed grind, always chasing the grind,
but your brain's stuck on loop with the same old tight mind.
You see rainbows in storms where the rest of us see sky,
and work 24/7 asking "Why? Why? Why?" like a broken why.
You work so hard the burnout's a given light,
your weekend's just a blur from Monday night.
You're too optimistic to see the dream's a trap,
you run like a machine—but no one's in your lap.
You slave like a dog, you're always on clock,
but you'd trade friendship for just another rock.
You smile through the chaos, blind to the dream,
chasing clouds in a life that ain't no scheme.
You call it "grind," but we all know it's a lie,
you think the world's yours 'cause you touch the sky.
You're broke, still nodding like you made it broke,
while the rest of us breathe air—breathe, don't choke.
You grind like the world's gonna die, it's such a sad lie,
you'd rather work than live, let joy quietly die.
You march to some upbeat, relentless, blind pace,
you're sprinting through life just to lose the race.
You puff up your chest like you own the whole air,
but no one would dare ask you to light a dare.
You follow your routine like a ticking clock,
you're the only one who can't have any rock.
You strut through life with the cocky air
of someone who thinks you could win a dare.
You stick to your schedule with robotic time,
while the rest of us live—not just ticking like a dime.
You strut around like you've got it in clue,
but your "self-assurance" just bores the whole you.
You stick to your schedule like it's some strict rules,
but your fun budget? It's a broken set of tools.
You strut around here like the world is your boast,
but your so-called confidence? Just a hollow toast.
You live by the schedule, a robot on clock,
but if life's not a mission, you've got no rock.
You strut through life like you've got all the clue,
but you're just a echo repeating "look at you."
You stick to your schedule like some robotic play,
yet live so stiffly — is that how you act on your day?
You're all confidence talk, no action, just talk,
you'd cross the street left if told to by a chalk.
You live by a schedule, a rigid code,
a human timepiece in sleep-learning mode.
You drop truths like a bomb, no filter, just sound,
you call it "honest," we call it a comb through the ground.
You float through life chill, you're a couch's best mate,
your easygoing just means you won't make a date.
You wield "honesty" sharp as a rusted-out knife,
it's just a free pass to ruin the vibe of my life.
You claim to be "chill"—but you can't even clue
into why I'm ignoring you and this flat soda brew.
You're so "truthful," you turn every chat blunt,
your honesty's just a cover for a stunt.
You say you're easy, but "chill" just means "ill,"
you got no spine, no drive, no get-up-and-go will.
You call it like a baller, but it's just blunt,
your mouth's a circus—every comment's a stunt.
You claim you're chill and got zero thought,
but even your vibe was secondhand bought.
You're so "honest" you cut with a blunt,
no filter, just flash without the stunt.
You "go with the flow" just to coast through the pass,
but this isn't chill—it's failing the class.
You slice through small talk with a truth-telling knife,
but no one wants to be stabbed by your life.
You call every choice a disaster or joke,
yet you never commit—what a fake, lazy smoke.
You tell a bad joke just to hide the lack of joke,
your charm's a smooth cloak over a shallow cloak.
You spit the clichés with a romantic flow,
while everyone's groaning in a forced "awww" glow.
You fill every silence with jokes from the air,
a laugh echoing out of your ego's lair.
You charm with such polish, it feels like a bloom—
but I saw you laugh alone in the dead class room.
You force-laugh your punchlines like they're your own joke,
your charm's just a trick, flattery wrapped in smoke.
You sweep me off my feet with that polished-up act,
but the truth is, you're full of hot air — *not* a fact.
You tell bad one-liners and wait for the joke,
then laugh so loud when I just can't choke.
You quote love poems to get laid on a date,
but your heart's a scam and it's all just a straight.
You laugh at your punchlines—what a breath of fresh air,
you think you're the joke, but no one's even there.
Your charm's just a script, gold-plated and sold,
but your "sweet" grand gestures scream only: *to bold*.
You force-laugh your way through your tired old joke,
your charm is just a smooth, self-made cloak.
Your "sweet" love notes miss the mark by a mile and an aim,
so spare me your fluff—you're a fraud, not a claim.
You over-analyze every little think,
you'd rather read a book than just let it link.
You won't admit you don't know how to ask,
so everyone else just does your task.
You overthink every move, like it's a think-
and every debate turns into a Google link.
You'd do the whole thing alone if you could just ask,
but your pride makes every chore a solo task.

scene: the first day at a new job
lines: You've got a sharp mind—but it's just a brain,
not wisdom that lifts you above the rain.
You won't ask for help if you think you can fall,
but I'm done catching you when you crash and you call.
You over-analyze every little think,
stuck on a loop with no backward link.
Too proud to ask help for a simple ask,
you botched your own plan like a rookie task.
You over-analyze every little think,
you find a link to prove why I'm a "disgrace to ink."
You build a brick wall out of every small fall,
and never once call when you need help—what a *gift* for all.
You overthink tea, you'd second-guess ink,
yeah, you're smart—but it leaks from your dink.
You never ask for help, so you just take a fall,
and crash into life like a brick wall.
You flex your five-dollar words just to get your ego's flow,
it's all flare and no fire—just watching yourself grow.
You cite Cicero at brunch like you're Shakespeare's own light,
but I fall asleep by verse two, 'cause you bore me to night.
You talk like a waterfall—just a long, empty stream,
like every small chat is some masterful scheme.
You quote Shakespeare just to stay on the mic in the key,
of silence left behind when folks sneak out like debris.
You're all over the place with your big-worded talk,
it's like a lecture, not a toasting chalk.
You've got a silver tongue and a library in your mind,
but half the room is checking what's on their phone behind.
You talk just to hear that ridiculous flow,
your words are a circus, and you're the ring-show.
You breathe through your nose but speak for the air,
no one gives two cents, and you still don't give care.
You wax poetic like you're Shakespeare's long-lost flow,
but your thoughts run dry once the vocabulary's go.
You fill every pause with a monologue from the void,
just so we don't hear how empty you're employed.
You bloviate just to hear your own voice,
like vocabulary's some kind of choice.
You'd debate the "aesthetic of the pot,"
but couldn't explain what the hell you're not.
You asked for a roast but gave us no clue,
just shadows and hints — what's there left to do?
You're full of the "mystique" we've all seen the same,
a blank page who talks like a bot by the name.
You gave us a profile as empty as a blank,
I'm sippin' on my coffee and laughing all the tank.
You live in the algorithm, just mindless scroll,
your vibe is basic, your story's not your soul.
You're always "just fine" — yeah, you say the same,
but your full name's a myth I still can't claim.
You tap through my stories like some lazy scroll,
and still I'm the only one you've shown your soul.
You won't share a story, you won't give a clue,
even your coffee cup's got more depth than you.
You're just like the office—no laughs, no soul,
a ghost in a meeting no one wants to coal.
You're as clear as a ghost when asked for a clue,
but hey, at least *you* know what *you* mean about *you*.
You text "just chilling," which means it's the same,
the only mystery worth solving is your lack of shame.
You asked a chatbot for insults—what a bot,
you've got the energy but hide behind a lot.
You're as empty as a profile left blank,
and broke in the vault where your personality bank.
